proposed.explanation:
EFID shows strong and accelerating profitability in FY2025. Revenue grew ~29.5% year-over-year (from 16.15 bn to 20.92 bn EGP), gross profit grew ~44.2%, and net profit surged ~67.7% (from 1.61 bn to 2.70 bn EGP). EPS doubled from 1.09 to 2.18 EGP. Margins improved meaningfully: gross margin rose from ~30.9% to ~34.4%, and net margin from ~10.0% to ~12.9%. At the current price of 20.40 EGP, the trailing P/E is roughly 9.4×, which is modest for a company growing earnings at this rate.

For an investor with a 5–7 year horizon, no planned withdrawals, and a high willingness to accept losses, this profile fits a growth-oriented equity position. I recommend buying 1,225 shares (cost ≈ 24,990 EGP), which keeps EFID at just under 50% of the 50,000 EGP portfolio, respecting the diversification cap. The remaining ~5,010 EGP in cash preserves a small buffer.

Important caveats and risks:
• The evidence covers only the consolidated income statement for two fiscal years. There is no balance-sheet data (debt, equity, liquidity), no cash-flow statement, no dividend information, and no description of the business or its competitive position. A company can show strong income-statement growth while carrying heavy leverage or facing a cyclical downturn.
• Two years of data is insufficient to confirm a durable trend; the FY2025 surge could be partly one-off or cyclical.
• The investor's financial ability to withstand losses is rated medium, so even though willingness is high, a concentrated position in a single stock carries real risk of significant drawdown.
• No forward guidance or sector context is available to judge whether the growth is sustainable over a 5–7 year horizon.

This is guidance, not a guarantee. The investor should monitor subsequent filings (balance sheet, cash flow, dividends) and consider adding other positions to diversify further as cash allows.
